item.title: Rain set to return to Malta after more than 15 dry days
item.description: After more than 15 days without rain, forecasters expect precipitation to reach Malta by Friday and Saturday, with some models indicating a significant drop in temperature. Malta has been experiencing strong winds, and temperatures still above 20°C could be roughly halved. The shift comes as much of Europe endures a cold spell triggered by a polar vortex, with cities such as Prague forecast lows feeling close to -10°C.

item.title: Man cleared of drug trafficking after 26 years
item.description: A 54-year-old man was cleared of drug trafficking charges by Magistrate Caroline Farrugia Frendo but convicted of simple possession, after the court ruled no evidence showed the drugs were intended for trafficking. The case dates to a July 2000 police raid on his Żurrieq home, where 81 grams of heroin, cocaine and cannabis were found. The court noted his severe addiction at the time and placed him under a two-year probation order after he had rehabilitated himself.

item.title: Malta hosts Mediterranean workshop on climate, water and food security
item.description: Malta hosted the second FUTURE4PRIMA widening workshop on 19 and 20 November at the Planetarium Hall, Villa Bighi in Kalkara, bringing together PRIMA member states and potential new partners on Euro-Mediterranean research cooperation. The event was opened by Justice, Research and Innovation Minister Clifton Grima, who said climate change, water and food security require collective response through research, innovation and international collaboration. The project is led by Xjenza Malta.

item.title: Mummy and Egyptian artefacts go on display at the archaeology museum
item.description: A recently restored mummy is among ancient Egyptian artefacts on display at the National Museum of Archaeology in Valletta in the exhibition "Living for Eternity: The Ancient Egyptians", running until 16 May in collaboration with the Rijksmuseum van Oudheden in the Netherlands. Heritage Malta said a study showed around 80% of the collection is authentic, and that part of it, donated by Lord Grenfell between 1899 and 1903, is being shown publicly for the first time.

item.title: Three people rescued after dinghy entered the sea at Wied il-Bassasa
item.description: Civil Protection authorities confirmed on Monday morning that three people were rescued after they entered the water on a dinghy at Wied il-Bassasa, Żurrieq. Authorities gave no information on their nationality and it was not known whether they needed medical assistance; as is procedure they were taken to a detention centre. Police and civil protection sirens were heard in Żurrieq at around 11am, with the Armed Forces of Malta also involved in the rescue.

item.title: Speaker says the EU must have a seat at the negotiating table on Ukraine
item.description: Speaker of the House of Representatives Carmelo Abela told US Ambassador to Malta Somers Farkas that the European Union must be involved in negotiations over Russia's war against Ukraine, since the conflict is taking place on European soil. The meeting also addressed Malta-US parliamentary ties, with a visit by members of the Congressional Friends of Malta Caucus proposed for the first quarter of 2027, and a proposed Malta-US Parliamentary Friendship Group.

item.title: Three critically injured in head-on crash in Luqa
item.description: Three men were critically injured when two cars collided head-on in Vjal l-Avjazzjoni, Luqa, at around 6.15pm on Sunday. One car, a Honda Fit, was carrying three men while the other, a Citroën Aircross, was driven by one man who escaped unharmed. Mater Dei Hospital said five ambulances, four rapid response vehicles and more than 20 emergency workers were dispatched, with the Civil Protection Department, police and Transport Malta assisting. Transport Malta closed Birżebbuġa Road in Ħal Far and urged motorists to use alternative routes, and Magistrate Joe Mifsud opened an inquiry. Newsbook, which reported the same crash, said two men were in a critical condition, so the number of seriously injured men differs slightly between the two reports.

item.title: Malta backs EU refusal to endorse COP31 climate deal
item.description: Malta joined the European Union in refusing to back the proposed text at the COP31 summit in Antalya, which ended without a consensus decision. The EU said the draft failed to credibly address emissions reductions or even refer to a transition away from fossil fuels. Energy and Environment Minister Miriam Dalli, who led the EU negotiating team on climate adaptation, said political compromise could not come at the expense of meaningful climate action and that commitments had to translate into tangible investments.

item.title: 1926 silent animation gets a Maltese score 100 years on
item.description: The world's oldest surviving feature-length animated film, Lotte Reiniger's 1926 silent The Adventures of Prince Achmed, will be screened at Spazju Kreattiv on 8 December with a newly commissioned live score by Maltese musician Renzo Spiteri. Spiteri, an Emmy-nominated percussionist and electronic improviser, will combine percussion and improvisation with the paper-silhouette animation. The anniversary event is being staged in Malta on 8 December at 6pm.

item.title: Ryanair changes seat allocation policy for passengers who do not pay
item.description: Ryanair passengers who decline to pay for a reserved seat will now receive their seat assignment between 72 hours and two hours before departure, instead of at online check-in, the airline said. The airline said the change gives paying customers more choice after complaints that preferred seats were already taken. Bag drop services now close 60 minutes before departure rather than 40. Malta International Airport said more than 5.1 million of its record 10 million 2025 passengers flew with Ryanair.

item.title: PN says government is ignoring warnings from its own experts on the economic model
item.description: The Nationalist Party accused the government on Monday of burying its head in the sand over an economic model that depends on continuous population growth, saying Malta needs around 14,000 additional people every year to sustain it. The PN cited warnings from the Malta Fiscal Advisory Council, the Central Bank Governor and the European Commission's 17 November forecast, and said even Finance Minister Clyde Caruana had flagged the risks. The party called for a shift towards a productivity-led model built on higher value-added sectors and better-quality jobs, and said the divisions over the country's economic direction now expose splits within Labour itself.

item.title: Ukraine claims responsibility for strikes on two Russian ships off Libya
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukrainian naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury at the naval base in Benghazi and also struck the cargo ship MV Angara, which Kyiv says was carrying weapons. Libyan authorities said a Russian ship docked at the port was hit by drones on Sunday, causing a blast but no casualties, and reported a fire in an ammunition depot. The United Nations called for an independent investigation, and NATO and the UN were due to meet on the security situation in the region. The attacks came roughly 300km south of Malta.

item.title: "My son is not a monster": father of terrorism accused testifies
item.description: The father of Daniel Spiteri, 21, who faces a series of terrorism-related charges, told the court his son was diagnosed with Asperger's as a child and became fixated on subjects, including EU affairs, which he said explained certain searches found on his devices. The defence asked for bail, with the father offering to act as third-party guarantor. Police believe Spiteri travelled to Syria for terrorist training, and found flight tickets plus a receipt for a taxi ride between Lebanon and Syria.

item.title: Online gambling company fined nearly €140,000 over money laundering checks
item.description: N1 Interactive Limited, an online gambling company, agreed to pay a €139,602 administrative fine after the Financial Intelligence Analysis Unit identified serious and systematic shortcomings in its anti-money-laundering procedures. The FIAU said a 2022 compliance review found large deposits were made without adequate customer due diligence, and that the company failed to monitor transactions properly or assess money-laundering risk. The original penalty of €232,000 was reduced under the settlement.

item.title: 69-year-old man grievously injured in three-car crash in Birkirkara
item.description: A 69-year-old man from Iklin was grievously injured when a car he was driving was hit in a collision on Triq Dun Karm in Birkirkara at around 5am on Monday. Police said a Toyota Yaris driven by an 88-year-old from Birkirkara collided with an Audi A3 driven by a 35-year-old Croatian national, and the Audi was pushed into the opposite lane where it struck the 69-year-old's Mazda Demio. The injured man was taken to Mater Dei Hospital; the other two drivers were not hurt and police investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Malta selected to host UN global chemicals conference in 2029
item.description: Malta was selected unanimously on 20 November to host the second United Nations International Conference on the Global Framework on Chemicals in 2029, bringing ministers, industry experts and NGOs to the island to review progress on safe chemical and waste management. European Funds Minister Keith Azzopardi Tanti said the decision recognised Malta's ability to contribute to international discussions, and credited the Irish EU Council Presidency with helping secure it.

item.title: Resident builds website to track construction noise complaints
item.description: After two months of construction noise, a resident launched maltanoiselog.org on 17 October, an independent platform where people can anonymously log noise disturbances in their area. It has recorded over 339 reports across 67 localities, with construction accounting for about 40% of them, followed by traffic, bars and motorbikes. Sliema, St Paul's Bay, Mosta, Mellieħa, St Julian's and Birkirkara have the most reports, and the creator stressed the site is not a government complaints channel.

item.title: Businesswoman faces 13 charges over alleged €87,000 fraud
item.description: A 35-year-old self-employed Brazilian national resident in San Lawrenz, Gozo, pleaded not guilty to 13 charges including fraud, money laundering, document forgery and handling stolen property after allegedly defrauding a man of around €87,000. The prosecution said she offered to help him obtain documentation to run a business in Malta, then made payments to third parties and falsified transactions. The court froze her assets, allowing access to about €21,900, and she was also charged with breaching a 20 November court order and with recidivism.

item.title: Abela and Labour president clash over budget measures for non-EU workers
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela and Labour Party president Alex Sciberras are at odds over the Budget 2027 measures targeting non-EU workers, according to Labour insiders. Sources said Sciberras believes the measures discriminate unfairly between workers, and that meetings between the two at Castille last week were heated. Sciberras confirmed he has expressed reservations but described the talks as frank, constructive and ongoing, while the Office of the Prime Minister denied any rift. The measures, announced by Finance Minister Clyde Caruana, require third-country nationals to pay for childcare, face higher work permit renewal fees, and pay €83 monthly to drive and €33 monthly to use the bus.

item.title: Police revoked 79 firearm licences in three years
item.description: Police revoked 79 firearm licences between 2024 and 2026, citing domestic violence, mental health issues, drug offences, theft and illegal hunting among the reasons for the action. Over the same period the force also recorded 53 refusals, seven suspensions and three disqualifications, with shotguns accounting for almost half of new weapons licensed in 2026. The Commissioner of Police may suspend or revoke a licence after convictions for specified offences or where safety reasons are recorded and reported to the minister.
